messages:
mike: Quick sync — thinking about a refactor to add a thin tenant connectivity abstraction so the control plane (CP) can be agnostic to how customer egress is wired. Idea: a single ConnectivityBinding API that either a private endpoint or our tenant gateway implements. Keeps CP <-> data plane surface small.

sarah: short version — CP only needs to reach a stable logical address and a small handshake. sounds promising. what's in the contract? :thinking:

mike: minimal fields: binding_id, expected_hostnames, auth_method (mtls/token), health_probe_path, fallback_order. optional metadata for latency/cost hints.

ben: curious about failure modes — if binding points at a regional gateway and that gateway fails, does CP retry to alternate region? what about preserving source IP for customer whitelists?

mike: good Q. plan is: binding includes an ordered list of endpoints (region + priority). CP will try primary, then fallback. source-IP preservation is orthogonal; the gateway decides whether to SNAT or preserve original based on binding flags. CP only signals intent.

anuj: do we need DNS vs IP? customer firewall rules typically require IP ranges. suggestion: bindings expose both a logical hostname and an ASN/IP-range hint array so ops can present a single downloadable CIDR set.

maria: rollout concerns: we have thousands of tenants. we need a migration path from per-tenant peering to binding model. propose a dual-mode: support legacy peering until tenant flips to binding. do we need a small data-migration job?

jess: for canary, we can enable binding on a few non-prod tenants and use traffic shadowing. Also recommend a per-binding health-check that reports probe latency and TLS cert fingerprint for quick validation. :+1:

mike: sketch of a toy JSON contract below — keeps it intentionally tiny so lib code is trivial.

```
{
  "binding_id": "bind-12345",
  "hostnames": ["cp-control.prod.redwood-tenant-1.internal"],
  "endpoints": [
    {"region": "us-west-2", "addr": "10.0.5.11", "priority": 0},
    {"region": "us-east-1", "addr": "10.1.7.9", "priority": 1}
  ],
  "auth_method": "mtls",
  "health_probe": "/.well-known/tenant-binding/health",
  "preserve_source_ip": "optional",
  "metadata": {"cost_category":"dedicated-gw","latency_slo_ms":"50"}
}
```

ben: that looks fine. one thought: metadata as freeform can be abused — maybe whitelist keys we care about to keep implementation sane.

anuj: security — who issues client certs for mtls? CP or tenant gateway? we should centralize issuance in CP for short-lived certs, with a rotation webhook so gateways can fetch new certs without operator intervention.

maria: operationally we need: (1) migration API, (2) binding liveness dashboard, (3) exportable CIDR pack for customers. also add audit entries when a binding flips.

mike: agree. I'll draft an RFC with: contract fields, handshake sequence, failure semantics, migration steps, and rollout checklist. aiming to present Thurs 10am.

jess: can you include a small e2e test plan? smoke -> failover -> rotate cert -> verify probe.

mike: yes. will include.

deploy-bot: mike triggered draft-rfc/tenant-connectivity-abstraction in #architecture (PR: https://git.internal/repos/rfcs/123)

mike: thanks — ping me if you want to review the draft before Thurs.
